_note: Quotations marked and cited in the text (BUG-632). Wording shared only inside such a quotation does not confirm an originality match: quoting a source with its citation is the honest way to use it. A quotation counts only when a citation sits beside it, because most quotation marks in a thesis are not quotations (button labels, section titles, code). Symmetric marks (") are paired by orientation: an opening mark follows a space or bracket and precedes a word; a closing mark follows a word. Single quotation marks are not listed: they cannot be told apart from apostrophes. after_words / before_words: how many words may separate the quotation from the start of a citation after it, or from the end of a citation before it. symmetric_opening_mark_follows / symmetric_closing_mark_precedes: the character that may come before an opening symmetric mark, or after a closing one, besides the start or end of the text. citation_search_chars: how far before and after a quotation a citation is looked for; keep it longer than before_words / after_words words plus the longest citation. A numeric citation directly after a word or bracket (date[0]) is code, not a citation. Patterns are Python regular expressions.
